wayBelowNormal.description: Rainfall is more than 60% below the seasonal average (<40% of normal rainfall)

belowNormal.description: Rainfall is 21% to 60% below the seasonal average (41% to 79% of normal rainfall)

nearNormal.description: Rainfall is within 20% of the seasonal average (80% to 120% of normal rainfall)

aboveNormal.description: Rainfall is more than 20% above the seasonal average (>120% of normal rainfall)

dryCondition.title: Dry Condition
dryCondition.definition: Two (2) consecutive months of below normal rainfall conditions (21% - 60% reduction).
dryCondition.recommendedAction: Begin monitoring soil moisture; check irrigation schedules and local advisories.

drySpell.title: Dry Spell
drySpell.definition: Three (3) consecutive months of below normal rainfall (21% - 60% reduction) OR two (2) consecutive months of way below normal rainfall (>60% reduction).
drySpell.recommendedAction: Implement water conservation measures; prepare supplemental irrigation; adjust planting calendars.

drought.title: Drought
drought.definition: Three (3) consecutive months of way below normal rainfall (>60% reduction) OR five (5) consecutive months of below normal rainfall (21% - 60% reduction).
drought.recommendedAction: Activate municipal crisis response; enforce strict water rationing; release emergency agricultural relief.

stages.status: Conditions are favorable for El Niño development
stages.probability: 50% or greater chance within the next 6 months
70% or greater chance within the next 2 months

stages.status: El Niño conditions are actively present and established
stages.probability: Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) at or above +0.5°C and expected to persist

heatIndexCategories.effects: Fatigue is possible with prolonged exposure and activity. Continuing activity could lead to heat cramps.
Heat cramps and heat exhaustion are possible. Continuing activity could lead to heat stroke.
Heat cramps and heat exhaustion are likely; heat stroke is probable with continued activity.
Heat stroke is imminent. Immediate intervention and strict avoidance of sun exposure required.

TypeI.name: Type I
TypeI.characteristics: Two pronounced seasons: dry from November to April; wet during the rest of the year.
TypeI.elNinoVulnerability: Very High during prolonged dry seasons (Dec-May).

TypeII.name: Type II
TypeII.characteristics: No dry season with a very pronounced maximum rain period from December to February.
TypeII.elNinoVulnerability: Moderate; Pacific moisture provides partial buffer, but winter monsoon can weaken.

TypeIII.name: Type III
TypeIII.characteristics: Seasons not very pronounced: relatively dry from November to April and wet during the rest.
TypeIII.elNinoVulnerability: High; moderate rainfall baselines leave little tolerance for 30%+ deficits.

TypeIV.name: Type IV
TypeIV.characteristics: Rainfall is more or less evenly distributed throughout the year.
TypeIV.elNinoVulnerability: Moderate; absence of a regular dry season makes sudden rain failure disruptive.
